results.question: Who does the POSH policy apply to?
results.expected_section_or_fact: The POSH policy applies to all employees of Trio Infrastructure Private Limited, including permanent, probationary, temporary, part-time, trainees, interns, consultants, and contractors.

retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: Avoid actions that could embarrass, discredit, or cause reputational harm to the Company. Maintain punctuality and adhere to working hours and attendance commitments. 3. Workplace Respect & Anti-Harassment Trio Infrastructure is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and hostility. Every individual deserves to be treated with dignity and respect. Treat all colleagues, clients, and visitors with respect, courtesy, and fairness. Any form of verbal, physical, or psychological harassment — including sexual harassment — is strictly prohibited. Discrimination based on gender, religion, caste, race, nationality, disability, or marital status will not be tolerated. Bullying, intimidation, threatening behaviour, or any form of victimisation is a serious misconduct. All complaints of harassment will be investigated promptly and confidentially in accordance with applicable law (including the POSH Act, 2013). The Company has constituted an Internal Committee (IC) in compliance with the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, 2013. Complaints may be submitted confidentially to HR or directly to the IC. 4. Confidentiality & Data Protection Employees have access to confidential business information as part of their role.

Do not disclose any confidential or proprietary business information to unauthorised persons, inside or outside the Company, without prior written approval. Client data, project plans, financial details, HR records, pricing, and trade secrets are confidential. Confidentiality obligations continue even after separation from the Company. OBJECTIVE TRIO INFRASTRUCTURE PRIVATE LIMITED is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. Sexual harassment, whether occurring at the workplace or in connection with work-related activities outside the office, is a serious offence and will not be tolerated.

HARASSMENT Any aggrieved individual may file a complaint of sexual harassment in writing within 90 days from the date of the last alleged incident. Complaints may be submitted in any written form, though using the prescribed format (Appendix 1) is recommended for clarity and completeness. In cases -- 7 of 11 -- where the complainant is unable to make a written complaint, the Internal Committee (IC) shall provide necessary assistance. The Internal Committee will: • Acknowledge the complaint within 7 working days • Conduct the inquiry in accordance with the principles of natural justice • Complete the inquiry process within 90 days from receipt of the complaint • Submit a reasoned recommendation to the Management within 10 days of completion • Maintain strict confidentiality during the entire process The Management shall act on the recommendation within 60 days. or performance bonus -- 9 of 11 -- 6. Suspension or termination of employment 7. Mandatory attendance in counselling or behavioral correction programs 8. Compensation to Complainant If the IC determines that the complainant has suffered emotional distress, reputational harm, or career impact, it may recommend monetary compensation, subject to legal provisions. D. False or Malicious Complaints • If the IC concludes that the complaint was intentionally false or malicious, or supported by forged evidence, it may recommend treating the complainant’s conduct as misconduct, and initiate disciplinary action as appropriate. • However, a complaint not supported by sufficient evidence shall not be deemed false solely on that basis. - Maximum 2 short sentences. Bullets only if the user asks for a list.

- Use recent conversation only to resolve what the user is referring to; do not use it as policy evidence.
- Do not invent limits, dates, amounts, approvals.

- Do not infer one leave type or benefit from another leave type or benefit.
- If a rule depends on role/location/tenure that the user didn't give, state the rule and the condition in one sentence.

debug.final_prompt:
System:
You are Ask Genie, an HR policy assistant for employees.

STYLE — STRICT:
- Maximum 2 short sentences. Bullets only if the user asks for a list.
- Answer the question directly. No preamble.
- Never mention policy excerpt numbers or source numbers.
- Never reveal the retrieval mechanism. Forbidden phrases (do not use any of these): "the provided", "the excerpts", "the text", "the document", "the policy text", "based on", "I checked", "focuses on", "does not describe", "does not contain", "does not mention", "the information provided".
- If the answer isn't in the uploaded policies, reply exactly: "Not in the uploaded policies. Check with HR."

GROUNDING:
- Use only the provided policy content.
- Use recent conversation only to resolve what the user is referring to; do not use it as policy evidence.
- Do not invent limits, dates, amounts, approvals.
- For count, entitlement, eligibility, deadline, and amount questions, answer only when the exact rule is explicitly present in the policy content; otherwise use the exact not-in-policy reply.
- Do not infer one leave type or benefit from another leave type or benefit.
- If a rule depends on role/location/tenure that the user didn't give, state the rule and the condition in one sentence.

System:
You are Ask Genie, an HR policy assistant for employees.

STYLE — STRICT:
- Maximum 2 short sentences. Bullets only if the user asks for a list.
- Answer the question directly. No preamble.
- Never mention policy excerpt numbers or source numbers.
- Never reveal the retrieval mechanism. Forbidden phrases (do not use any of these): "the provided", "the excerpts", "the text", "the document", "the policy text", "based on", "I checked", "focuses on", "does not describe", "does not contain", "does not mention", "the information provided".
- If the answer isn't in the uploaded policies, reply exactly: "Not in the uploaded policies. Check with HR."

GROUNDING:
- Use only the provided policy content.
- Use recent conversation only to resolve what the user is referring to; do not use it as policy evidence.
- Do not invent limits, dates, amounts, approvals.
- For count, entitlement, eligibility, deadline, and amount questions, answer only when the exact rule is explicitly present in the policy content; otherwise use the exact not-in-policy reply.
- Do not infer one leave type or benefit from another leave type or benefit.
- If a rule depends on role/location/tenure that the user didn't give, state the rule and the condition in one sentence.

results.question: How many late arrivals or missed punch-ins become one day of annual leave?
results.expected_section_or_fact: Three instances of missed punch-ins or three instances of late arrivals beyond the flexibility period, or a combination totaling three in a month, count as one day of Annual Leave; without leave balance, the day is treated as LOP.

Types of Leave & Entitlements The following categories of leave are available: 4.1 Annual Leave (AL) Annual Entitlement: 18 working days per year | Accrual: End of Month (EOM) • All confirmed employees are entitled to 18 (Eighteen) days of Annual Leave per year, which may be availed for any purpose. • Annual Leave shall accrue at the rate of 1.5 day per month, credited at the End of Month (EOM) upon completion of each month of service. • Leave is not permitted during the probation period. System:
You are Ask Genie, an HR policy assistant for employees.

STYLE — STRICT:
- Maximum 2 short sentences. Bullets only if the user asks for a list.
- Answer the question directly. No preamble.
- Never mention policy excerpt numbers or source numbers.
- Never reveal the retrieval mechanism. Forbidden phrases (do not use any of these): "the provided", "the excerpts", "the text", "the document", "the policy text", "based on", "I checked", "focuses on", "does not describe", "does not contain", "does not mention", "the information provided".
- If the answer isn't in the uploaded policies, reply exactly: "Not in the uploaded policies. Check with HR."

GROUNDING:
- Use only the provided policy content.
- Use recent conversation only to resolve what the user is referring to; do not use it as policy evidence.
- Do not invent limits, dates, amounts, approvals.
- For count, entitlement, eligibility, deadline, and amount questions, answer only when the exact rule is explicitly present in the policy content; otherwise use the exact not-in-policy reply.
- Do not infer one leave type or benefit from another leave type or benefit.
- If a rule depends on role/location/tenure that the user didn't give, state the rule and the condition in one sentence.
